Definition: from G1487 and G5037; if too:--if, or, whether.
BiblicalUsage: Whether is the word that covers both sides, and Paul uses it to say that the answer is the same either way. Whether you eat or drink, do all to the glory of God, whether we are Jews or Gentiles we are all baptised into one body, and whether there are prophecies, they shall fail, but love never fails. The word holds the choices together and lets love decide them.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe whether is God's way of saying the details do not divide us, because the same Lord covers both sides of every honest choice. Love is the rule that settles what whether leaves open.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
